section_summary: This section documents U.S. processing of requests for entry into occupied Japan by merchants, foreign nationals, clergy, and accompanying family members, including applications, theater clearances, permit correspondence, telegrams, and documentary waivers. Several duplicate sets concern David and Rosette Mehrez’s proposed Egyptian trade mission, while other substantial cases involve Y. I. E. Assia, Robert Liewer, Banwari Lal, Victor Kelly Bashi, and Morteza Nouriani. The section concludes with a Commerce Department list of approved applicants and additional individual application forms.

subfiles.title: Application for permission to visit Japan — Victor Kelly Bashi
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Bashi applies to visit Tokyo to develop import and export business.
subfiles.summary: Business-travel application listing commodities handled, Tokyo as the destination, and notarization by Harry Rosenthal.

subfiles.title: War Department record concerning a Japan military permit
subfiles.about: Records military-permit correspondence routed to the Division of Protective Services.
subfiles.summary: Mostly illegible War Department routing record dated March 18.

subfiles.title: Return of U Myun’s unused military permit
subfiles.about: Reports that U Myun was recalled to Burma and cannot use his Japan permit.
subfiles.summary: Chappell returns U Myun’s military permit because the Burmese government recalled him.

subfiles.title: Reply to the Egyptian Embassy concerning Isaac Cohen’s application
subfiles.about: Explains referral of Cohen’s application and a faster British-protection procedure for future Egyptian applicants.
subfiles.summary: The Department says Isaac Cohen’s case was sent to Army authorities and recommends routing future Egyptian applications through British protecting-power channels in Japan. It cites the earlier Joseph Gassute case.

subfiles.title: Buenos Aires airgram concerning a business-travel applicant
subfiles.about: Transmits biographical and commercial information on an Argentine applicant seeking individual business travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Buenos Aires reports on an Argentine business-travel applicant under the Department’s 1947 procedures; much of the applicant’s name and supporting detail is illegible.

subfiles.title: Request to reissue Banwari Lal’s permit for May
subfiles.about: Requests extension or replacement of Banwari Lal’s expiring permit for travel in May.
subfiles.summary: Business commitments in India prevented Lal from using Permit 8202; his company requests May validity.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Military Permit 9272
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of a Japan entry permit and waiver of the exit-permit requirement.
subfiles.summary: The permit holder confirms the planned itinerary and promises to report any delay.

subfiles.title: Conversation concerning Victor Kelly Bashi’s rejected application
subfiles.about: Records Commerce follow-up after Bashi’s application was deferred pending information about his previous departure from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Commerce will contact Bashi and obtain details about his exit from Japan on an earlier trip.

subfiles.title: Army request for further information on Victor Kelly Bashi
subfiles.to: Division of Protective Services, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests information needed to reconsider Bashi’s Japan-entry clearance.
subfiles.summary: Army asks State to obtain additional facts about Bashi’s previous departure from Japan.

subfiles.title: Application for permission to visit Japan — Victor Kelly Bashi, duplicate
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Bashi seeks to visit Tokyo to establish trade in textiles, industrial goods, and Asian products.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate application describing Bashi’s firm, merchandise, proposed Tokyo visit, and lack of prewar Japanese business.

subfiles.title: Instructions for a new Banwari Lal application
subfiles.about: Explains that Lal must file a new Commerce application because his permit cannot be extended through May.
subfiles.summary: Chappell requests return of Permit 8202 and submission of a fresh application specifying May entry.

subfiles.title: Telephone inquiries concerning Robert Liewer’s clearance
subfiles.about: Records Agnes Curran’s requests for a clearance telegram to Robert Liewer in Saigon.
subfiles.summary: Curran asks State to cable Liewer’s Saigon address after receipt of his theater clearance.

subfiles.title: Telegram notifying Robert Liewer of Japan clearance
subfiles.about: Directs the consul to notify Liewer that he may enter Japan for business in April.
subfiles.summary: Liewer receives a sixty-day entry clearance and instructions concerning passport photographs and certification.

subfiles.title: Telegram notifying Ezra of Japan clearance
subfiles.about: Reports clearance of a Syrian business executive named Ezra for April entry into Japan.
subfiles.summary: The consul is to furnish Ezra a certified clearance text for a sixty-day stay.

subfiles.title: War Department military-permit memorandum
subfiles.about: Conveys military-permit information for several applicants.
subfiles.summary: Most applicant names and substantive instructions are illegible in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Conversation concerning Y. I. E. Assia’s itinerary
subfiles.about: Records Assia’s flight schedule and the planned waiver of his exit permit.
subfiles.summary: Assia will fly from San Francisco through Honolulu to Japan; State will waive his exit permit.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Military Permit 9901 to Y. I. E. Assia
subfiles.about: Encloses Assia’s permit and asks for departure details needed to waive his exit permit.
subfiles.summary: Permit 9901 authorizes one return journey to Japan during April 1948.

subfiles.title: Cairo submission of applications for David and Rosette Mehrez
subfiles.about: Forwards Egyptian diplomatic notes and applications for David and Rosette Mehrez to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Egyptian Foreign Ministry endorses the Mehrez trip to revive commerce, particularly exports of cotton and salt to Japan. David Mehrez proposes business consultations in Tokyo and Osaka; Rosette Mehrez applies to accompany him. The package includes the French note, English translation, and duplicate application forms.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Cairo submission for the Mehrez applications
subfiles.about: Duplicates the embassy memorandum, Egyptian note, and translation supporting the Mehrez applications.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate set endorsing David and Rosette Mehrez’s proposed commercial trip to Japan to promote Egyptian cotton and salt.

subfiles.title: Second duplicate Cairo submission for the Mehrez applications
subfiles.about: Provides another copy of the Cairo memorandum and the Egyptian Foreign Ministry note and translation.
subfiles.summary: Another duplicate set concerning the Mehrez couple’s approved Egyptian commercial mission to Japan.

subfiles.title: Third duplicate Cairo submission for the Mehrez applications
subfiles.about: Provides a further duplicate of the Mehrez visa memorandum and diplomatic-note enclosures.
subfiles.summary: Further duplicate documentation for the Mehrez applications, emphasizing Egyptian cotton and salt exports.

subfiles.title: War Department notice of S. A. Hamoui’s clearance
subfiles.about: Reports the terms of Hamoui’s authorization to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hamoui is cleared for April entry and a stay of sixty days.

subfiles.title: Notification to the Syrian Legation concerning S. A. Hamoui
subfiles.about: Notifies Syria that Hamoui may enter Japan and explains the required passport endorsement.
subfiles.summary: State reports Hamoui’s clearance for April entry and a sixty-day stay, requesting that the prescribed SCAP statement be placed in his passport.

subfiles.title: Cancellation of E. W. Frazar’s immediate Japan trip
subfiles.about: Cancels Frazar’s April voyage because of illness and discusses Mrs. Du Mars’s resulting change of plans.
subfiles.summary: Frazar hopes to travel later; Mrs. Du Mars may instead seek a position with General Eichelberger.

subfiles.title: Illegible file index card
subfiles.about: Records an unidentified filing or transfer action.
subfiles.summary: Mostly illegible file card concerning a transfer or filing action.

subfiles.title: Emergency telegram concerning Assia’s missing permit
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Asks SCAP to assist Assia if he reaches Japan before his delayed permit arrives.
subfiles.summary: State confirms Assia’s clearance and explains that his permit was airmailed to Honolulu before his April 3 flight.

subfiles.title: Delay in mailing Y. I. E. Assia’s military permit
subfiles.about: Documents recovery and air-mailing of Assia’s delayed permit to Honolulu.
subfiles.summary: The signed letter had stalled in clearance; Corkran retrieved the permit and mailed it to Pan American Airways in Honolulu.

subfiles.title: Telephonic waiver for Y. I. E. Assia
subfiles.about: Waives Assia’s exit-permit requirement for his March 30 departure.
subfiles.summary: Exit-permit waiver for Assia’s TWA flight from San Francisco.

subfiles.title: Conversation concerning permits for Fathers Kircher and Thora
subfiles.about: Records efforts to issue Japan permits after both priests received theater clearance.
subfiles.summary: The priests were flying from Brazil and would contact State after reaching the United States.

subfiles.title: Conversation concerning George Terk’s departure
subfiles.about: Records George Terk’s departure details and planned exit-permit waiver.
subfiles.summary: Terk was to leave Minneapolis April 1 aboard Northwest Airlines Flight 801.

subfiles.title: War Department memorandum concerning a Japan permit
subfiles.about: Responds to a permit or clearance inquiry involving travel and business in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The damaged text refers to a prior cable and commercial activity in Japan.

subfiles.title: Commerce transmittal of approved Japan applicants
subfiles.about: Transmits a list of applicants approved by Commerce, subject to SCAP’s final approval.
subfiles.summary: Cover memorandum forwarding approved applicants and copies of foreign nationals’ applications.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Commerce transmittal of approved applicants
subfiles.about: Duplicates the Commerce memorandum forwarding approved Japan-travel applicants.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate cover memorandum for the attached approved-applicant list.

subfiles.title: List of applicants approved by Commerce for travel to Japan
subfiles.from: Department of Commerce, Office of International Trade
subfiles.about: Lists companies, applicants, nationalities, and desired Japan-entry dates approved by Commerce.
subfiles.summary: The list covers numerous American, Japanese, Chinese, Belgian, and Greek business applicants and records preferred entry dates, onward travel, or prior Japanese visits. OCR damage obscures several names, but entries include Ivan F. Baker, Jean P. Boyer, Victor Shalem, Elmer C. Harrison, and others.

subfiles.title: Telegram announcing Morteza Nouriani’s Japan clearance
subfiles.about: Authorizes Nouriani to enter Japan during June for a sixty-day business stay.
subfiles.summary: The embassy is to give Nouriani a certified clearance text and instructions concerning passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Application of Morteza Nouriani for permission to enter Japan
subfiles.from: Randall S. Williams, American Embassy, Tehran
subfiles.about: Submits Nouriani’s trade application for referral to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Nouriani seeks Japanese porcelain, glassware, celluloid goods, and cotton piece goods and reports substantial prewar trade with Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Referral of Morteza Nouriani’s application to the Army
subfiles.about: Requests Army transmission of Nouriani’s trade application to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Chappell quotes the Tehran Embassy’s account of Nouriani’s commercial interests and prewar Japanese business.

subfiles.title: Return of Morteza Nouriani’s military permit
subfiles.about: Returns Nouriani’s permit after notifying the Tehran Embassy of his clearance.
subfiles.summary: State returns Military Permit 114 and confirms that Tehran was informed by cable.

subfiles.title: War Department permit memorandum
subfiles.about: Conveys military-permit action, apparently connected with pending Japan travelers.
subfiles.summary: Most substantive text is illegible; the record is dated April 2.

subfiles.title: Conversation concerning permits for Fathers Thora and Kircher
subfiles.about: Records Father Anderson’s request for urgent permits before the priests’ April 9 sailing.
subfiles.summary: Both priests had theater clearance and were flying from Brazil; Anderson held San Francisco ship reservations for them.

subfiles.title: Return of Banwari Lal’s expired permit
subfiles.about: Returns Lal’s expired Permit 8202 and acknowledges that a new application is required.
subfiles.summary: The company returns the March permit for replacement through a fresh Commerce application.

subfiles.title: Application for permission to visit Japan — Robert L. Liewer
subfiles.from: Robert L. Liewer and North American Continental Company
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Liewer applies to visit Japan to expand the company’s agricultural, textile, and industrial trade.
subfiles.summary: The application describes the company’s international affiliates, prewar Indochina–Japan rice and maize trade, recent transactions, and need for Liewer’s presence to develop Japanese commerce.

subfiles.title: Blank application for permission to visit Japan
subfiles.about: Provides an unused two-page form for Japan-travel applications.
subfiles.summary: Blank Commerce application requesting business history, destinations, agents, and purpose of travel.

subfiles.title: Application for permission to visit Japan — Werner Karl Kirchholtes
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Kirchholtes applies to restore prewar contacts and develop automotive, machinery, steel, and textile trade with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Kirchholtes describes Transmares Corporation’s business, his German birth and pending citizenship, prewar textile imports, and proposed import-export development.

subfiles.title: Application for permission to visit Japan — Banwari Lal
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Lal applies for business travel involving yarns, textiles, equipment, minerals, and other goods.
subfiles.summary: First page of Lal’s application, describing his company, commodities, and affiliated firms’ prewar Japanese trade.
